questions.text: Which method converts a JSON string into a JavaScript value?
options: JSON.parse()
JSON.stringify()
JSON.toObject()
JSON.read()
questions.explanation: JSON.parse() reads JSON text and returns the corresponding JavaScript value.

questions.text: What does Array.isArray([1, 2, 3]) return?
options: true
false
undefined
questions.explanation: Array.isArray() returns true when its argument is an array.

questions.text: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned?
options: let
const
static
export
questions.explanation: let declares a block-scoped variable whose value can be reassigned.

questions.text: What value does the expression 5 === '5' produce?
options: false
true
It throws a TypeError
questions.explanation: Strict equality does not coerce values, and a number is not equal to a string.

questions.text: Which built-in Node.js module provides the createServer() function used to make a basic HTTP server?
options: http
path
events
crypto
questions.explanation: The built-in http module provides createServer() for creating HTTP servers.

questions.text: What does the fs.promises API generally return for an asynchronous file operation?
options: A Promise
A worker thread
A synchronous file descriptor only
An EventEmitter for every operation
questions.explanation: The fs.promises API exposes promise-based file-system operations that can be awaited.

questions.text: In a CommonJS module, what does module.exports determine?
options: The value made available to modules that require() this module
The Node.js version used by the process
The package manager's lockfile format
The environment variables inherited by child processes
questions.explanation: module.exports defines the exported value returned by require() for that module.

questions.text: Which method registers a listener for an event emitted by a Node.js EventEmitter?
options: on()
listenOnce()
addRoute()
watchFile()
questions.explanation: EventEmitter.on() registers a listener that runs when the named event is emitted.

questions.text: What does path.join() do when given multiple path segments?
options: Combines them into a normalized path
Reads the file at the resulting path
Changes the process working directory
Converts the path to a URL
questions.explanation: path.join() joins path segments and normalizes the resulting path.

questions.text: How can a Node.js program read an environment variable named PORT?
options: process.env.PORT
process.config.PORT
node.env.PORT
module.env.PORT
questions.explanation: Node.js exposes environment variables through the process.env object.

questions.text: What does setImmediate() schedule in Node.js?
options: A callback to run in the check phase after I/O callbacks
A callback to run before the current JavaScript stack finishes
A callback to run only after a one-second delay
A new operating-system process
questions.explanation: setImmediate() schedules its callback for the event loop's check phase.

questions.text: Which Buffer method creates a Buffer from a string using a specified encoding?
options: Buffer.from()
Buffer.allocUnsafeString()
Buffer.read()
Buffer.encode()
questions.explanation: Buffer.from(string, encoding) creates a Buffer containing the encoded string data.

questions.text: In a CommonJS module, what does require.resolve() return?
options: The resolved filename for a module without loading its exports
The module's exported object
The package version from the lockfile
A Promise for the module contents
questions.explanation: require.resolve() resolves a module specifier to its filename without loading the module.

questions.text: Given a compound index on { tenantId: 1, createdAt: -1, status: 1 }, which query can use the index prefix without constraining createdAt or status?
options: A query filtering on tenantId
A query filtering only on status
A query filtering only on createdAt
A query filtering on status and createdAt but not tenantId
questions.explanation: Compound indexes support leading prefixes, so tenantId alone can use the first index field.

questions.text: In a sharded MongoDB cluster, what is a primary purpose of choosing a shard key with high cardinality and even value distribution?
options: To help distribute data and write load across shards
To guarantee every query is a scatter-gather
To remove the need for indexes
To make every document reside on every shard
questions.explanation: A well-distributed shard key helps avoid hotspots by spreading data and workload across shards.

questions.text: What does a $lookup stage with a pipeline and let variables enable that a simple localField/foreignField lookup does not express as directly?
options: Correlated joins with pipeline conditions on the foreign collection
Automatic schema validation on both collections
A transaction spanning unrelated clusters
A unique constraint across both collections
questions.explanation: A pipeline-based $lookup can use let variables and $expr to apply correlated conditions to foreign documents.

questions.text: What does the majority write concern require for an acknowledged write?
options: Acknowledgment after the write is committed by a majority of voting data-bearing members
Acknowledgment from every client connected to the cluster
Replication to every shard regardless of the write target
A successful read from every secondary before the write begins
questions.explanation: Majority write concern waits for acknowledgment that the write has been committed by a majority of voting data-bearing replica-set members.

questions.text: Which transaction property ensures that a transaction's changes are applied as one indivisible unit?
options: Atomicity
Eventual consistency
Sharding
Document validation
questions.explanation: Atomicity means a transaction's operations succeed together or are rolled back together.

questions.text: What does the executionStats mode of explain() provide?
options: Execution details and statistics for the query plan
A permanent index on every queried field
A snapshot of all documents in the collection
A guarantee that future runs use the same plan
questions.explanation: The executionStats verbosity executes the winning plan and reports execution details such as examined keys and documents.

questions.text: What is a key property of a partial index?
options: It indexes only documents that satisfy its filter expression
It stores only the first field of every document
It automatically expires documents after a fixed interval
It can be used only by aggregation pipelines
questions.explanation: A partial index contains entries only for documents matching its specified filter expression.

questions.text: How does a TTL index affect documents whose indexed date has expired?
options: MongoDB removes them asynchronously in the background
MongoDB immediately archives them to another collection
MongoDB rejects reads that match them
MongoDB converts them to capped collection records
questions.explanation: The TTL monitor removes expired documents asynchronously rather than at an exact deadline.

questions.text: In an update with upsert enabled, when does $setOnInsert apply?
options: Only when the operation inserts a new document
For every matched document before $set runs
Only when the update matches multiple documents
Only after the document is deleted
questions.explanation: $setOnInsert assigns fields only when an upsert creates a new document.

questions.text: What must a client do to consume MongoDB change stream events?
options: Open a change stream on a supported replica set or sharded cluster
Enable capped collections on every database
Create a TTL index on the event timestamp
Run the server with standalone storage only
questions.explanation: Change streams are available on replica sets and sharded clusters and provide a cursor for event consumption.

questions.text: What does the $merge aggregation stage do with pipeline results?
options: Writes the results into a specified collection
Combines two replica sets into one
Creates a compound index from each result
Streams results directly to every connected client
questions.explanation: $merge writes aggregation output documents into a target collection.

questions.text: When does a multikey index become useful?
options: When indexing a field whose value is an array
When encrypting a field with multiple keys
When a query reads from multiple replica-set members
When a collection contains multiple databases
questions.explanation: MongoDB creates a multikey index when an indexed field contains array values.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a shard zone in a sharded cluster?
options: To associate key ranges with selected shards
To encrypt documents according to their shard key
To ensure every query is routed to all shards
To reserve an index namespace for one database
questions.explanation: Zones associate shard-key ranges with designated shards to support data placement policies.

questions.text: What does readConcern: 'snapshot' provide for reads inside a transaction?
options: A consistent snapshot of data at a single point in time
The newest value independently from each replica-set member
A lock that prevents all other writes until the transaction ends
A permanent snapshot collection created for the transaction
questions.explanation: Snapshot read concern provides a consistent view of data at a single point in time for the transaction.
